The proposed solution imposes the extra restriction \(a=b\).  
While the condition \(\gcd(a+b,2025)=1\) (i.e. \(\gcd(a+b,2025)=1\)) is indeed necessary for the sums \(i+j\pmod{2025}\) to take all residues, it is **not** necessary that the two step‑sizes be equal.  

When \(\gcd(a+b,2025)=1\) one can choose the sequence of “row’’ versus “column’’ moves so that, for each diagonal value \(u\), the set of rows taken on odd steps and the set taken on even steps are disjoint and together cover all \(2025\) rows. This yields a Hamiltonian path without requiring \(a=b\).  

Consequently the count of admissible pairs is larger than the \(\varphi(2025)=1080\) pairs obtained by forcing \(a=b\). The final answer \(1080\) is therefore incorrect.  

**Verdict:** REJECT.
